resources.string: LEAKCAM Setup
Connect your LEAKCAM to Wi-Fi in four steps. The phone talks to it over Bluetooth, so stay within a few metres of it.
1. Plug the LEAKCAM into USB power
2. Find it
3. Enter your Wi-Fi network
4. Pair, check and save
Find LEAKCAM
Wi-Fi name (SSID)
Wi-Fi password
Show password
Pair, check and save
Save without checking

Plug the LEAKCAM into a USB charger or a computer with its USB-C cable. It can be set up only while it is on USB power: someone has to plug it in first, so it cannot be paired while it runs on its battery. Then tap Find LEAKCAM.
Looking for LEAKCAM boards nearby…
No LEAKCAM found. Check that it is plugged into USB power and within a few metres, then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
No LEAKCAM found. Check that it is plugged into USB power and within a few metres, and that Location is on (this Android version needs it for Bluetooth scanning), then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
Pick your LEAKCAM (the one with the strongest signal is usually the nearest), then enter the Wi-Fi network it should use.

Enter the name and password of the Wi-Fi network the LEAKCAM should use. It must be a 2.4 GHz network: the LEAKCAM does not see 5 GHz. If your router shows separate names for the two bands, pick the 2.4 GHz one. Leave the password empty for an open network. Then tap Pair, check and save: the LEAKCAM tries the network before it keeps it.
Connecting to %1$s…

Your phone now asks to pair with %1$s.

• Tap Pair (on some phones: Allow or OK).
• There is no PIN to type: the LEAKCAM has no screen or buttons.
• If no request appears, pull down the notification shade and tap the Bluetooth pairing notification.

Pairing is needed only once. It keeps the Wi-Fi password encrypted on its way to the LEAKCAM.
%1$s is already paired with this phone. Sending the Wi-Fi settings…
Paired. Sending the Wi-Fi settings…
The LEAKCAM is now joining "%1$s" to check the name and password. This takes up to a minute; keep the phone near it.
Password accepted. Getting an address from the router…
Connected to the router. Checking that the internet can be reached…
Done. %1$s joined \"%2$s\", reached the internet and stored the network.\n\nYou can unplug it now. It connects at its next scheduled check.
Saved without checking. %1$s stored the Wi-Fi network \"%2$s\".\n\nIt tries the network at its next scheduled check. If it never reports, plug it in where the network reaches and set it up again.
This phone has no Bluetooth, which the setup needs.
Allow Bluetooth access (Nearby devices) so the app can find the LEAKCAM, then tap again.
Bluetooth access allowed. Tap again to continue.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then tap again.
Scanning failed (error %1$d). Turn Bluetooth off and on, then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
Tap Find LEAKCAM and pick your board first.
The Wi-Fi name must be 1 to 32 characters long.
The Wi-Fi password must be 8 to 63 characters long, or empty for an open network.
The LEAKCAM did not answer. Check it is still plugged into USB power and nearby, then try again. If a pairing request is still open on the phone, accept it first.
The LEAKCAM disconnected (status %1$d). Keep it on USB power and nearby, then try again.

Pairing did not go through.

• Was the request declined, or did it time out? Try again and tap Pair.
• Is the LEAKCAM on USB power? It refuses pairing on battery.

The LEAKCAM no longer recognises this phone (it was reset, or paired again elsewhere).\n\nOpen the phone\'s Bluetooth settings, tap %1$s, choose Forget (or Unpair), then tap Pair, check and save again.

The LEAKCAM cannot see "%1$s".

• Check the name: upper and lower case count.
• It must be a 2.4 GHz network.
• The router may be out of reach from where the LEAKCAM is now. If you are setting it up elsewhere, use Save without checking.
The router refused the password for \"%1$s\" (code %2$d). Check the password (upper and lower case count) and try again.
The router did not let the LEAKCAM join (code %1$d). It may limit how many devices can join, or allow only known devices. Check the router\'s settings and try again.
The password is right, but the router gave the LEAKCAM no address. Check that the router hands out addresses (DHCP) and try again.
The LEAKCAM is on the network, but internet names do not resolve. Is the router connected to the internet?
The LEAKCAM is on the network, but it cannot reach the internet. Is the router connected to the internet?
This network shows a login page or filters traffic (answer %1$d). The LEAKCAM cannot log in to such networks: use one without a login page, such as your home network.
The LEAKCAM is busy: its cameras are running after a leak alarm. Wait a minute and try again.
The LEAKCAM could not store the settings. Try again; if it keeps failing, the board needs service.
The LEAKCAM reported an unexpected result (%1$d). Try again.
The connection to the LEAKCAM dropped during the check. Nothing was stored. Keep the phone close to it and try again.
This device is not a LEAKCAM in setup mode. Keep it on USB power and scan again.
The LEAKCAM refused the %1$s (error %2$d). Check it and try again.
Could not send the %1$s. Try again.
